idiom_name: tagged plain object + handler Map (structuredClone / JSON envelope)
implementation_notes: JavaScript cannot serialise behaviour, so the command base disappears: a command is a plain `{ kind, payload }` object and `execute` is a handler looked up on the receiving side in a Map keyed by `kind`. Inside one process or across worker_threads the structured clone algorithm (postMessage, structuredClone) carries the object; across machines it is JSON (or a binary codec) over a socket or a queue. Functions, classes and prototypes never cross the boundary, so a 'command class' must be reduced to data plus a name before sending - which is exactly what the pattern demands, not a workaround.
pitfalls: JSON.parse resurrects __proto__ as an own property, and plain-object registries hit inherited keys: look handlers up in a Map (or an Object.create(null) table) and treat an unknown kind as a protocol error.

structuredClone and JSON drop or reject what the language allows - functions disappear, class instances lose their prototype, Date becomes a string, Map/Set/undefined vanish - so the wire shape must be plain JSON-compatible data validated before dispatch.

Back-pressure is the sender's problem: a queue with unbounded concurrency accepts commands faster than the invoker can deserialise them, and there is no constructor to enforce invariants on the far side.
